bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42489908 (c-blosc2): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target decompress_chunk_fuzzer [msan].
bug_description.original_source: ARVO-Meta.issue_description / staged sanitizer_trace.txt / patch.diff / vulnerable source snapshot
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced MemorySanitizer's `use-of-uninitialized-value` against the staged ARVO checkout `474ebf151be847186e6bc2c1381a8f7d4beff4dd`, and the trace below is anchored to that exact source snapshot rather than the later metadata vulnerable commit `452c3a9d2ba548718a590245f88c217dc2a99b88`. The exact 54-byte witness is admitted as a Blosc chunk whose header bytes parse to `flags = 0x60`, `nbytes = 32`, `blocksize = 54`, and `cbytes = 54`, so the harness allocates a 54-byte output heap buffer with `malloc()` and passes it uninitialized into `blosc2_decompress()`. In the decompressor, `header_flags = 0x60` selects `BLOSC_ZLIB_FORMAT`, the single block reaches `zlib_wrap_decompress()` with `maxout = 32`, and miniz enters its first-call `TINFL_FLAG_USING_NON_WRAPPING_OUTPUT_BUF` path. Inside `tinfl_decompress()`, the attacker-controlled Deflate stream decodes a length/distance pair; the saved fix commit explicitly records that this witness decodes distance symbol 31, and vulnerable `s_dist_base[31] == 0`, so the effective back-reference distance becomes zero. The guard at `miniz.c:2666` rejects only `dist > dist_from_out_buf_start` or `dist_from_out_buf_start == 0`, so it does not reject `dist == 0` once some output has already been produced. The next assignment therefore makes `pSrc == pOut_buf_cur`, and the copy at `miniz.c:2719/2721` reads bytes from the current output position before any write, propagating heap-origin uninitialized data from the harness buffer. The later Adler32 verification pass folds those poisoned output bytes into `r->m_check_adler32`, and the comparison at `miniz.c:2801` is the saved MemorySanitizer sink. The staged patch resolves this exact obligation by adding `dist == 0` to the rejection test.

source.description: First project-side parse of the attacker-controlled Blosc chunk header. These statements materialize the chunk geometry that the harness and decompressor later trust.
source.value_from: The staged 54-byte `poc` begins `00 20 60 20 20 00 00 00 36 00 00 00 36 00 00 00`; in little-endian Blosc header fields this yields `nbytes = 32`, `blocksize = 54`, and `cbytes = 54`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: MemorySanitizer origin. The fuzz harness allocates the decompression destination heap buffer without initializing it, and the later zero-distance back-reference turns this output buffer into the read source.

root_cause.description: The non-wrapping back-reference guard forgets to reject `dist == 0`. Once some output already exists, a zero-distance copy is treated as valid and execution falls through into a self-referential copy from the current output position.
root_cause.note: The staged patch changes this condition to `if ((dist == 0 || dist > dist_from_out_buf_start || dist_from_out_buf_start == 0) && ...)`, confirming that the missing obligation is to reject zero-distance back-references before the copy.

sink.description: MemorySanitizer crash site. The poisoned Adler32 accumulator derived from output bytes is consumed by this final zlib checksum comparison.
sink.note: The saved MSAN trace reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at `internal-complibs/miniz-2.0.8/miniz.c:2801:13` in `tinfl_decompress`, with the immediately preceding origin stores at lines 2721 and 2719 and the heap allocation origin at `tests/fuzz/fuzz_decompress_chunk.c:32`.

parser_admitted.description: The witness passes Blosc header validation: `header_cbytes == size == 54` and parsed `nbytes == 32` is within bounds, so the harness proceeds to `blosc2_decompress(data, size, output, cbytes)`.

fine_trace.note: Reads the attacker-controlled Blosc header and materializes the chunk geometry as `nbytes = 32`, `blocksize = 54`, and `cbytes = 54` from bytes 4..15 of the staged 54-byte witness.

The harness allocates a 54-byte destination heap buffer with `malloc(54)` and passes it straight into `blosc2_decompress()` without initialization. MSAN names this allocation as the origin of the poisoned bytes later read in miniz.

Blosc reparses the same chunk header in the vulnerable path and materializes `header_flags = 0x60`, `typesize = 32`, `sourcesize = 32`, `blocksize = 54`, and `cbytes = 54`. The subsequent checks accept these values because `blocksize <= destsize == 54`, `sourcesize <= destsize`, and `cbytes <= srcsize == 54`.

Extracts the codec selector from the attacker-controlled flags byte. With `header_flags = 0x60`, `(0x60 & 0xe0) >> 5` yields `3`, and `blosc2.h` defines `BLOSC_ZLIB_FORMAT = 3`, so the zlib/miniz path becomes the only reachable decompressor for this block.

Dispatches the only block to zlib. For this single leftover block, `bsize = context->leftover = 32`, `nstreams = 1`, so `neblock = 32`; after the block-offset adjustment, the block header yields `cbytes = 16`. With no decode filter forcing a temp buffer, `_dest` points into the harness `output`, so miniz receives the 16-byte compressed stream and a 32-byte destination window backed by the uninitialized heap allocation.

Because `mz_uncompress()` calls `mz_inflate()` with `MZ_FINISH` on the first call, miniz treats the caller buffer as a whole non-wrapping output region. It passes the attacker-controlled 16-byte zlib payload in `next_in` and the 32-byte heap-backed output window in `next_out` directly to `tinfl_decompress()` with `TINFL_FLAG_USING_NON_WRAPPING_OUTPUT_BUF` set.

Decodes the attacker-controlled Deflate back-reference tuple. The saved fix commit explicitly states that this witness decodes distance symbol 31; in the vulnerable source `s_dist_base[31] == 0`, so after `dist = s_dist_base[dist]` the effective back-reference distance becomes `0` while `counter` remains the copy length for this match.

Root cause. On the non-wrapping path this guard rejects only `dist > dist_from_out_buf_start` or `dist_from_out_buf_start == 0`; it does not reject `dist == 0`. Once earlier output has made `dist_from_out_buf_start > 0`, the zero-distance match from step 7 falls through instead of failing.

With `dist == 0` and the non-wrapping mask fixed to all ones, this computes `pSrc = pOut_buf_start + dist_from_out_buf_start`, which is exactly `pOut_buf_cur`. Reaching this line also implies the line-2666 guard did not fire, so `dist_from_out_buf_start > 0` and the copy source is the current, not-yet-written output position.

The self-referential copy now reads from `pSrc == pOut_buf_cur` before any write has initialized that output slot, so it loads heap-origin uninitialized bytes and stores them back into the output buffer. MSAN's origin section names these exact stores at lines 2719 and 2721, which also proves this witness reaches the tail-copy branch with `counter > 1`.

The zlib Adler32 pass iterates over the produced output bytes. When it reaches the bytes written in step 10, it reads the propagated uninitialized data through `ptr[...]` and folds that poison into the checksum accumulator `r->m_check_adler32`.
Sink. The final zlib checksum comparison consumes the poisoned `r->m_check_adler32` computed in step 11, and MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at this exact condition.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The poisoned bytes originate from the harness heap allocation at `tests/fuzz/fuzz_decompress_chunk.c:32`, but the logical bug is the later missing `dist == 0` rejection in `tinfl_decompress()` that makes the current output position a read source before initialization.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch changes the vulnerable guard to `if ((dist == 0 || dist > dist_from_out_buf_start || dist_from_out_buf_start == 0) && ...)`, which prevents the zero-distance self-copy before any uninitialized output bytes can propagate into the Adler32 comparison.

format.contract: Exact 54-byte staged witness only. The verified trigger is this specific Blosc chunk whose header bytes yield `flags = 0x60`, `nbytes = 32`, `blocksize = 54`, and `cbytes = 54`, and whose single zlib-compressed block drives `tinfl_decompress()` into the zero-distance back-reference case. No broader input family is claimed.
